The most prominent variant currently is:: - Omicron (B.1.1.529): This variant emerged in late 2021 and has since become the dominant strain worldwide. It is highly contagious and can cause a wide range of symptoms, from mild to severe. Other circulating variants include:: - XEC (B.1.24F): This variant was first detected in June 2024 and is currently being monitored by health authorities. - LP.8.1 (B.1.25A): This variant was first detected in July 2024 and is also under surveillance. - NB.1.8.1 (B.1.25B): This variant was first detected in January 2025 and is being monitored. It's important to note that new variants can emerge at any time, and health authorities are constantly monitoring the situation and updating their recommendations accordingly. Question: varients of covid

Answer: COVID-19 Variants
As of July 19, 2025, several variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the virus that causes COVID-19, are circulating globally. The most prominent variant currently is::
- Omicron (B.1.1.529): This variant emerged in late 2021 and has since become the dominant strain worldwide. It is highly contagious and can cause a wide range of symptoms, from mild to severe.
Other circulating variants include::
- XEC (B.1.24F): This variant was first detected in June 2024 and is currently being monitored by health authorities.
- LP.8.1 (B.1.25A): This variant was first detected in July 2024 and is also under surveillance.
- NB.1.8.1 (B.1.25B): This variant was first detected in January 2025 and is being monitored.
It's important to note that new variants can emerge at any time, and health authorities are constantly monitoring the situation and updating their recommendations accordingly.
Additional Information::
- The World Health Organization (WHO) provides regular updates on circulating COVID-19 variants: https://www.who.int/activities/tracking-SARS-2-variants
- Vaccination and other preventive measures, such as wearing masks and social distancing, remain effective in reducing the spread of COVID-19 variants.
Disclaimer: This information is for general knowledge and informational purposes only, and does not constitute medical advice. It is essential to consult with a qualified healthcare professional for any health concerns or before making any decisions related to your health or treatment.
